hints: Notice point P is at a trough of the solid curve, which is one of the two maximum-displacement shapes of the stationary wave.
Recall that amplitude $A$ means distance $A$ from the equilibrium position to either maximum, so opposite maxima are separated by $2A$.
Think what happens to all points in a stationary wave after half a period $T/2$ - each vibrating point reverses from one extreme to the opposite extreme.
walkthrough: Identify the starting position: the solid line shows P at its lowest point, a maximum displacement $A$ below equilibrium.
State the rule for a stationary wave: each point between nodes performs SHM with fixed amplitude, and the whole shape reverses every half period.
After time $T/2$ the oscillation phase changes by $180$ degrees, so a point at one extreme moves to the opposite extreme.
Therefore P moves from $-A$ to $+A$ relative to equilibrium, and the distance travelled is $A + A = 2A$.

options.A: P does not stay still. In a stationary wave every point except a node oscillates up and down with SHM.
options.B: $A$ is only the distance from equilibrium to one extreme, not the distance from one extreme to the opposite extreme.
options.C: P moves from maximum displacement $A$ on one side to maximum displacement $A$ on the other side, so total path is $2A$.
options.D: $4A$ would be the distance for a full oscillation from one extreme and back again, which takes one full period not half a period.
